walkthroughs.body_html:
Handling Data — a core area of GCSE Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Handling Data brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Handling Data.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which average is most affected by extreme outliers?
options: mean
median
mode
range

mcqs.q: What is 0.00307 written to 2 significant figures?
options: 180 degrees, the same as a triangle.
0.003, treating significant figures the same as decimal places.
0.00 — counting the first two digits after the decimal point.
0.0031 — leading zeros are not significant; the first two significant figures are 3 and 0.

mcqs.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of any pentagon?
options: 180 degrees, the same as a triangle.
540 degrees — use (n - 2) x 180 with n = 5.
Take the average of the probabilities on the branches.
360 degrees, because all polygons' angles sum to one full turn.

mcqs.q: On a probability tree, how do you find the probability of a sequence of outcomes along one path?
options: 180 degrees, the same as a triangle.
Take the average of the probabilities on the branches.
Multiply the probabilities along that path.
Add the probabilities along the path.
